guides.name: Claude
guides.difficultyWhy: Not an OAuth app. Do not try to register an OAuth app for Claude. Third party access is an API key from the Claude Console, with no OAuth approval queue.
guides.approvalWait: None. There is no OAuth approval stage for a Claude API key.
guides.accountNeeded: Claude Console account at platform.claude.com, separate from a claude.ai chat account, plus a payment method for API credits
guides.cost: Free to create a key. API use is billed per token from prepaid Console credits, separate from a Claude chat subscription.

steps.title: Create a Claude Console account
steps.detail: Sign in at platform.claude.com, or create an account. This is separate from claude.ai chat, with separate billing.
steps.blockerTip: A claude.ai chat login alone does not give you API access. Use the Console account.

steps.title: Add credits before testing
steps.detail: Open Settings, Billing, and check your balance before your first call. API billing is separate from a Claude subscription.
steps.blockerTip: At a zero balance, API calls will not work. Add credits first.

steps.title: Create one named API key
steps.detail: Open API keys, click Create key, name it after the app, choose an expiration, and choose a linked account. Use a service account key for a shared app, CI, or production service.
steps.blockerTip: If Create key is greyed out, your role cannot create keys. Ask an organization admin.

steps.title: Store the key safely, once
steps.detail: Copy the full key, starting with sk-ant-, straight into a secrets manager and set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The Console shows it only once.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the key in client code, a public repo, logs, or agent output. If you lose it, create a new key and delete the old one.

steps.title: Test one call, then stop
steps.detail: Send one test request with the key as a Bearer token. A 401 means a wrong, expired, or revoked key, or trailing whitespace. A multi workspace key must also send the workspace header.
steps.blockerTip: Do not reuse Claude Code or claude.ai OAuth tokens in another product. Those OAuth tokens are locked to Claude Code and Claude.ai.

guides.name: ChatGPT
guides.difficultyWhy: OAuth, but limited trial for commercial apps. Sign in with ChatGPT is a real OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flow, but commercial access is currently a limited trial, so approval is the blocker, not the code.
guides.setupTime: 2 to 4 hours for the sign-in code, plus unknown wait for commercial trial access
guides.approvalWait: Unknown. Commercial Sign in with ChatGPT is a limited trial. Contact an OpenAI representative. Do not promise a date.
guides.accountNeeded: OpenAI developer account, plus an approved OAuth client, typically beginning with oaiapp_, for commercial sign-in
guides.cost: Free to build. API use is billed separately. ChatGPT plan usage, where offered, has its own caps and is a separate flow from identity sign-in.
guides.consoleName: OpenAI Developers, Sign in with ChatGPT

steps.title: Pick the right ChatGPT path first
steps.detail: Use Sign in with ChatGPT for user identity. Use an API key for your own OpenAI API calls. Use the Apps SDK with your own authorization server for a ChatGPT app. Do not mix these three.
steps.blockerTip: If you need user identity, the API key path will not give it. If you need API calls, sign-in alone will not give it.

steps.title: Request an OAuth client, do not guess one
steps.detail: For a commercial app, join the limited trial through an OpenAI representative and get a client ID, an exact callback URL for each environment, and a token endpoint auth method. If you are not approved, stop here.
steps.blockerTip: A guessed client ID or callback URL will fail. The example client oaiapp_example is not a real client.

steps.title: Load OpenID discovery, do not hardcode endpoints
steps.detail: Load https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/openid-configuration and use the issuer, authorization endpoint, token endpoint, and JWKS URI from that document.
steps.blockerTip: If OpenAI changes an endpoint, hardcoded values break. Discovery is the source of truth.

steps.title: Build sign-in with PKCE on your backend
steps.detail: Create a fresh state, PKCE verifier and S256 challenge, and nonce on your backend, store them server side, and expire the transaction. Bind it to a server session cookie.
steps.blockerTip: Never create PKCE values or store the verifier in browser code. A reused or expired transaction must end sign-in.

steps.title: Add the Continue with ChatGPT button
steps.detail: Use approved OpenAI branding and the label Continue with ChatGPT, and add the data-oai-siwc-button attribute to the button so OpenAI can verify and troubleshoot it.
steps.blockerTip: Use the exact registered callback URL. A mismatch is a common first failure.

steps.title: Exchange the code and verify the ID token
steps.detail: On your backend, exchange the code at the token endpoint with the original redirect URI and PKCE verifier, then verify the ID token signature against the JWKS, and check issuer, audience, expiration, nonce, and subject. Then create your own session.
steps.blockerTip: For identity-only sign-in, do not require an access or refresh token. They are not part of the standard identity contract. Never put a client secret in client code.

guides.name: Composio
guides.difficultyWhy: Not a provider OAuth app. This guide is for a Composio auth config. Managed auth is easy, custom auth is medium because it needs a provider OAuth app and an exact Composio callback URL.
guides.setupTime: 30 to 60 minutes for managed auth, 1 to 2 hours for a custom auth config with a provider app
guides.approvalWait: None in Composio itself. Provider approval, where required, is separate and varies by provider.
guides.accountNeeded: Composio project account, plus a provider account if you create a custom auth config
guides.cost: Check current Composio pricing in the dashboard. Provider costs are separate.

steps.title: Start with managed auth
steps.detail: Use Composio managed auth for the toolkit first and test one connection. Go custom only for your own branding, custom scopes, dedicated quota, a custom instance, or a toolkit with no managed auth.
steps.blockerTip: Custom auth adds a provider app to maintain. Do not start there if managed already covers the toolkit.

steps.title: Get a project API key, server side only
steps.detail: In the dashboard, go to Settings, Project Settings, API Keys, copy the key, and store it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY in server secrets.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the project API key in browser code, chat, or a public repo. A CLI login alone does not export it for an app.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config
steps.detail: In the dashboard, click Create Auth Config, choose the toolkit, then go to Authentication management and Manage authentication with custom credentials.
steps.blockerTip: Check the toolkit auth scheme first. Some toolkits use API keys, not OAuth2.

steps.title: Register the provider app with the Composio callback
steps.detail: In the provider portal, set the authorized redirect URI exactly to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, then copy the provider client ID and client secret back.
steps.blockerTip: A mismatch here is the most common failure. The legacy URL https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add is still supported, but set the URL explicitly in both places.

steps.title: Finish the auth config and copy its ID
steps.detail: Select the OAuth2 scheme, toggle Use your own developer credentials, enter the provider client ID and secret, set Redirect URI to the registered URL, click Create, and copy the auth config ID, starting with ac_.
steps.blockerTip: Do not share the client secret. Store it in the auth config, not in code.

steps.title: Use the auth config in a session
steps.detail: Pass the auth config ID in authConfigs, keyed by toolkit, when you create a session. Toolkits you leave out keep managed auth. Store the connected account ID on your server and verify the connection before showing success.
steps.blockerTip: Creating an auth config alone does not change a session. If you do not pass its ID, the session still uses managed auth. For managed OAuth, use link or session authorize, not the retired managed initiate path.
